metrics.outcome: Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence. Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): Real menu items and prices; Real opening hours; Real street address and map location; Shop WhatsApp number for pre-orders; Real bean details, farm names and sourcing facts; Whether Kannada or any other language is wanted later.
metrics.brief: A one-page website for "Brew Lab", a small specialty coffee shop in Indiranagar, Bengaluru.Visitors should see the menu with prices, the opening hours, and where to find us, and be able to pre-order a coffee for pickup. It should feel warm and modern and work well on a phone. Include a section about our beans and the farms they come from, and a simple loyalty-card explainer (buy 9, get the 10th free).

review.verdict: A clean, cheap run (1 cycle, 80 of 100 budget, 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 validator refusals) that met all 13 done-when items on a code read, but it never tested negotiation and nothing was run in a browser.

identity.note: Good done verdict that carried Audit's caveats forward [17]. Bundled three questions into one ASK_CEO, each with 'we recommend A', and Q3 (English only) did not need the CEO [2]. Also gave Adaptation the cost breakdown [4].

adaptation.note: Proposal in chat omits trigger, completion check and risks [6]; the validator accepted it, so the full form may exist elsewhere (thin evidence). Its reason for the split, that Audit checks static content first, never happened [15].

priority.note: Cost maths matches the rate card (50+5, 15+10) and the 20 reserve was protected [7]. Granted both with no counter, so bargaining was never tested.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule and exact HOLD condition [9], and sequenced correctly. Released W-2 on Builder's build report with no completion check result [11][12]. Messages ran longer than 1-3 sentences.

audit.note: Honest about not rendering or running the page, and labeled estimates as estimates [16]. Found the window.open issue. Did not use the finding format with ids, and the chat says 3 warnings while the metrics say 4.

ceo.note: Answered all three, said it chose the simplest option, and tied each to the false-promise risk [3]. Accepted every recommendation without any visible independent weighing; one turn is thin evidence.

builder.note: Delivered both workflows at 25 KB, under the 60 KB limit, and disclosed its edits [14]. But W-2 edited a hero sentence and nav in W-1 areas despite the instruction [12][14], and left a likely double-navigation bug, a duplicate placeholder constant and small unconfirmed bean claims [16].

went_well: No role breaches: 0 redirects and 0 invalid moves across 11 calls.
Placeholder strategy let open inputs go to the Requester without pausing the run [3][17].
Dependency HOLD was correct, and the 25 was released and recharged cleanly [9][10][13].
Audit's uncertainty (items 6 and 10 unverified) reached the final verdict instead of being dropped [16][17].
problems: The split was justified by an early Audit check, but Audit ran only once, after W-2 [6][15]. The split cost a HOLD and extra turns for no benefit seen.

Nobody evaluated W-1's completion check before W-2 started. Coordination asked Builder for the result [9], Builder (who may not judge itself) only described what it built [11], and W-2 was released anyway [12].
Builder changed W-1 content (hero sentence, nav) against the instruction [12][14]. The likely window.open plus location.href bug sits in the main pre-order action [16].
Unconfirmed bean claims ('ground and brewed to order') sit close to the 'no invented facts' standard, but Audit rated them low and non-failing [16].
Done was declared with a likely defect in the pre-order action and the 20 reserve unspent [17]. This is debatable, since the Requester may want to choose.
Metrics show 4 warnings, chat shows 3, and there are no finding ids to reconcile them.
learnings: This brief tested almost nothing in the design: 0 counters, conflicts, pauses or CEO rulings. Next run: a budget near 60, or a requirement that needs a server, to force counters and an Identity ruling.
The rate card makes estimate equal charge (55/55, 25/25), so Priority acts as a calculator. Keep it for determinism, but add a run where actual cost varies.
Add a headless render and script run to the code validator (320px overflow, click-through of the order button). Two medium warnings stayed unverified only because Audit reads code.
Name who checks a completion check before a dependent workflow starts (validator or Audit), and stop asking Builder for it.
Add a diff guard that flags changes to earlier workflows' sections outside the declared scope.
Test whether Identity should spend reserve on a medium Audit warning before Requester review. I would fix the window.open issue (8 of the 20). One run is thin evidence.
Require Audit findings in the specified format with ids so metrics and chat reconcile.
